extractions.value: Examination revealed a stiff, swollen, abnormally postured left lower limb. His left foot was fixed in plantarflexion at the ankle, and his leg was hyper-extended and partially adducted at the hip. He could achieve only minimal flexion of his left knee. His gait was slow and painful with circumduction of his left leg and plantarflexion of the foot. Examination of both upper limbs and right lower limb was normal, including deep tendon reflexes. Plantars were flexor bilaterally. Reflexes could not be elicited in the stiff left leg but were seen to spread to the right side. There was no involvement of axial muscles of the thorax or abdomen.

extractions.value: First reported case of anti-GAD positive paraneoplastic stiff limb syndrome associated with renal cell carcinoma. Tumor specimen was not retained and therefore could not be tested for GAD expression. Steroids were avoided because of the patient's diabetes.
extractions.quote: Our report is the first to document a case of anti-GAD positive PSLS with a renal cell carcinoma. Unfortunately, tumor specimen was not retained in this case and therefore could not be tested for GAD expression. Steroids were avoided in our patient because of his diabetes and IVIG was tried instead.
